title: 1. Price and training scale
explanation: C is the published dividend/split-adjusted close. The chosen final market fit uses population standard deviation (ddof=0), frozen at the training cutoff. Raw volume is displayed for inspection but does not enter this chosen algorithm.

title: 2. Two parallel local-linear filters
explanation: j is fast or slow. F=[[1,1],[0,1]], H=[1,0], observation noise variance R, independent Gaussian slope innovation variance λR. Initial mean (log C₀,0), covariance R I. These are two estimates of the same price, not additive factors and not two interacting HMMs.

title: 3. Causal Kalman recursion
explanation: Only prices available through the current completed close enter the update. The first 252 observations initialize filtering before the HMM observations and likelihood scores begin.

title: 4. Updated level and slope
explanation: Fast and slow filters each have their own fitted R and λ. State estimates keep changing every day; their noise parameters remain fixed in the historical evaluation.

title: 5. Fit filter smoothness separately for each ETF
explanation: Slow λ∈[10⁻¹⁰,10⁻⁶]; fast λ∈[10⁻⁵,10⁻²]. Search log λ with bounded scalar minimization (tolerance .15, max 18 iterations), compare both endpoints. This fits price likelihood, not trading profit, and the allowed smoothness ranges are imposed.

title: 6. Slow context
explanation: pˢ_R=1−pˢ_D−pˢ_U; slow down means pˢ_D≥.70, otherwise context can be uncertain. Numerical slope variance is floored at 10⁻²⁰. Slow down does not veto buying a short rebound.

title: 7. Symmetric fast-state observation model
explanation: a∈[.2,2], v∈[.01,4], vR∈[.000025,.01]. D/R/U mean negative slope, near-zero slope and positive slope under this statistical model; R does not establish a geometric horizontal trading box.

title: 8. Forward HMM inference
explanation: At the first HMM observation (index 252), use the fitted initial distribution directly before normalization. Training may use backward probabilities; trading never does. Shared directional variance gives monotone up/down emission odds, but persistent transition priors can still dominate small new slopes.

title: 9. Fit symmetric emissions
explanation: γ and ξ are standard forward/backward training state/transition expectations. vR is the γR-weighted x² mean, clipped to [.000025,.01]. Denominators use a 10⁻¹² numerical floor. Two starts a=.2/.4, 25 iterations; retain the highest penalized training likelihood across starts and iterations.

title: 10. Fit transition persistence
explanation: Clamp each diagonal to [.65,.98] and rescale off-diagonals proportionally to keep each row summing to one. Update initial π=(γ₀+.1)/1.3. Initial T has diagonal .94/off-diagonal .03 and uniform π; directional variance starts as clip(sample population variance,.01,4), neutral variance .01.

title: 11. Entry, context and ordinary exit
formula: E_t=\mathbf{1}(p_{tU}\geq e)\mathbf{1}(\widehat b_{f,t}>0),\quad h_t=d+(.85-d)cA_t,\quad D_t=\mathbf{1}(p_{tD}\geq h_t)
explanation: Per-ETF e,d∈{.60,.75}; c is the inherited context flag. Protection multiple is kₜ=2k₀ if cAₜ=1, otherwise k₀, with k₀∈{3,5}. Every selected ETF now uses the symmetric fast HMM even if its inherited metadata says family=slope.

title: 12. Optional persistent thesis failure
explanation: Use only when the inherited per-ETF training-selected thesis rule is enabled; otherwise F=0. Candidate q∈{.1,.2,.3}, k∈{2,3}. The stronger slow-up tolerance applies to this thesis rule even if c=0. The run counts all observed closes, not just held sessions.

title: 13. Initial and ratcheting closing protection
explanation: Oe is the actual entry fill. Risk uses frozen training σ times entry price, not current ATR. While held, first test today's close against the previously adopted B; only then raise tomorrow's boundary. Existing boundaries never widen. B is a close-trigger boundary, not a resting intraday order or guaranteed loss cap.

title: 14. Position decisions and rearming
explanation: d is the desired binary position, initially zero. First set armed=true on rearm. If d=1 and X=1, set d=0 and armed=false. Else if d=0, actually flat, armed and E=1, set d=1 and armed=false. Otherwise retain d. Next-open lag is 1+Δ; Δ=0 primary, 1 stress. Pending target snapshots execute at their scheduled opens; a reversal can be scheduled before an earlier target fills. A range state alone is not an exit.

title: 15. Self-financing account
explanation: Buy with all available sleeve cash; sell all shares; f=5/10/20 bp per side. No leverage, cash interest zero, fractional adjusted units. Trading signals and close boundaries fill at later opens. First evaluation account starts flat/funded; filter history is carried. Terminal holdings are marked, not forcibly liquidated. No fixed TP, recovery override, Bayesian policy learner or learned return gate is active.

title: 16. Inherited policy fitting objective
explanation: g=CAGR, S=annualized daily Sharpe, K=CAGR/max(.03, drawdown magnitude) for the historical optimization only. Reported Calmar instead uses actual drawdown. The utility compares the training strategy with its ETF buy-and-hold under the original protocol.

title: 17. Stability and evidence penalties
explanation: Three equal chronological training blocks; n completed trades and eₓ exposure. Original 24 policies cover slope/HMM/context families × entry .6/.75 × exit .6/.75 × distance 3/5. Keep top two per family, then rescore six fee/delay settings; prefer candidates with ≥5 closed trades and ≥5% exposure in every setting, then highest worst-setting J. Exact selected parameter snapshots are retained; the symmetric HMM replaces the detector afterward without jointly retuning these thresholds.

title: 18. Portfolio ranking inputs — proposed next experiment
explanation: rᵢ is the net return of ETF i's continuously simulated chosen strategy, including cash days. Primary short/long horizons are 63/252 sessions; 21/126 is a declared sensitivity. At least Llong+1 causally generated NAV observations, two nonzero-return days, finite positive short and long SD; otherwise ranking unavailable. Flat zero-variance sleeves are not assigned infinite Sharpe. Cash rate remains zero for matched research.

title: 19. One combined rank table
explanation: Higher is better; average ranks handle ties, ticker breaks equal combined scores. M is the eligible risky pool size; BIL is a cash reference, not a ranked candidate. Monthly close selects top N without a positive-return gate; even the best ranks can be losing. N∈{6,10,15,20,30}, with 15 only an illustrative preview, not a chosen optimum.

title: 20. Equal capital and covariance of strategy risk
explanation: M_N=min(N,eligible count). Equal-weight and risk-weight budgets sum to one across selected strategy sleeves. Covariance includes cash observations and simultaneous losses. A 50% diagonal shrinkage and 5% annualized volatility floor prevent a nearly inactive sleeve receiving unbounded weight. These are declared engineering choices, not tuned portfolio results.

title: 21. Equal risk contribution, not inverse variance
explanation: This defines covariance-aware equal risk contribution. With diagonal covariance it reduces to inverse volatility, 1/√variance, not 1/variance. No leverage. Large N does not guarantee independent exposures; inspect effective number 1/Σw², correlations and sector/asset concentration.

title: 22. Membership, capital and actual exposure differ
explanation: Monthly allocation sets initial sleeve budgets. They then drift with each sleeve's returns; h is its actual binary invested state. A strategy sell moves that sleeve to cash. Do not renormalize other ETFs daily or replace a flat member before the next pool selection. Portfolio accounting must use actual fills, not both net sleeve returns and duplicate underlying trade fees.

title: 23. Timing sensitivity and broad-N preference
formula: D_t=\sum_{i\in\{ETFs,cash\}}|w^{\mathrm{theory}}_{i,t}-w^{\mathrm{last\ adopted}}_{i,t}|,\quad N^*=\max\{N:S_N\geq S_{best}-.05,\ g_N\geq g_{best}-.01,\ DD_N\leq DD_{best}+.02\}
explanation: Monthly membership is primary. A separate dynamic control adopts targets on monthly dates or cash-inclusive L1≥.10; it does not replace the monthly design. Daily signal exits always execute in both. Select N only inside chronological training/validation, preferring the largest acceptable performance plateau; report the full N curve and untouched subsequent results. If no robust plateau transfers, retain no performance claim.
